newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Finmeccanica move to pressure France.
newsitem.headline: Italy Finmeccanica move to pressure France.

text.p: Italy's radical shake-up at state-controlled defence group Finmeccanica is aimed at forging European alliances, and so will pressure France towards greater participation in defence consolidation, analysts said on Monday.

Strategic alliances that could be formed by Finmeccanica with other European nations, such as Britain and Germany, will undoubtably push France to hurry through its own industry restructuring and focus on European consolidation, they added.

Italian state holding IRI, which holds 60 percent of Finmeccanica, announced last week a restructuring to create a single operating unit to run the firm's industrial concerns, and Finmeccanica's chairman Fabiano Fabiani resigned.

Analysts said the move finally signalled the end of Italian hopes that Finmeccanica could be built up into an Italian defence and engineering conglomerate, and would now create a nimbler grouping to pursue vital European strategic alliances.

Last month, Finmeccanica signed a memorandum of understanding with Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC) to study opportunities in defence, and last week's move should make an Anglo-Italian deal easier to achieve.
"The British will clearly use this deal to try and put pressure on the French," said one defence industry analyst.

The French are still in the throes of making decisions on their own national industry consolidation with the bidding process for the state's 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF held up by French elections.
The final bidding process is expected to be decided by end-June with two main bids on the table, from Alcatel Alsthom together with Dassault Industrie, and from Lagardere Groupe.
Britain's GEC is in talks with both bidders to see whether it can join, and analysts say any deal with Finmeccanica will pressure the French to hurry along its defence consolidation.
Europe's fragmented defence industry is struggling to agree on areas for consolidation to compete with the U.S. defence industry which underwent restructuring in the early 1990s.
Finmeccanica has two major defence interests --defence electronics and its Alenia/Agusta aerospace arm.

In defence electronics, Finmeccanica has a business worth $1.5 billion of annual sales and a deal between Britain, Italy and France would form the core of defence electronics consolidation in western Europe, analysts said.

In aerospace, Alenia is part of the three-nation Tornado warplane consortium and the four-nation grouping for Eurofighter, while in civil aircraft it is part of an Franco-Italian venture producing turboprop planes -- a venture which has its links with British Aeropace.
Helicopter maker Agusta is currently in a joint venture with Britain's GKN Westland unit developing the EH101.

Analysts say closer European links could bring Alenia as a main sub-contractor into the four-nation Airbus consortium, but analysts see it unlikely Italy will become a main partner along with France, Germany, Britain and Spain.

"Finmeccanica clearly has a role to play in the consolidation of Europe's defence electronic interests, and we are starting to see the pressure mount on France to take part in that consolidation," said another industry analyst.

Finmeccanica made a 540.4 billion lire ($315 million) loss in 1996 after extraordinary writedowns of 575 billion lire for restructuring and for future investment as it moves towards eventual privatisation.

The managing director of Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana, Luigi Fausti, whose group holds 3.35 percent of Finmeccanica, said on Monday that the chairman of IRI had assured him Finmeccanica was hoping to be privatised this year, but many analysts believe this timetable is too short for the group.

Finmeccanica shares slumped on the opening of the Milan bourse, after the announcement late last week, but soon moved ahead up 3.78 percent at 960 lire by 1350 GMT in an overall lower market. ($1=1,716 lire)
